title: Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
content_md: Apache has patched a critical HTTP Server vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), following independent discoveries by Anthropic and Google researchers. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618 , the flaw affects Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The issue was addressed on November 11 with the release of version 2.4.71. It resides in mod_http2, the module responsible for handling HTTP/2 traffic. The vulnerability involves a race condition in which multiple threads improperly access shared resources, potentially corrupting server memory. According to Red Hat , an attacker could exploit the issue remotely without authentication to execute arbitrary commands and gain control of the server process. Red Hat assigned the vulnerability a CVSS score of 9.8 and explained that “only servers that have HTTP/2 enabled are affected; servers configured to serve only HTTP/1.1 are not vulnerable.” Apache credited Anthropic’s OSS Scanner with reporting the flaw on October 26. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research independently reported the same vulnerability on November 3. Cloud security firm Wiz reported that 64% of cloud environments in its data contained resources running affected Apache versions, while 51% had publicly exposed instances.
